# Book of Giants Fragment 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 4Q203 frag. 7 (Cave 4) | **Condition:** fragmentary; upper portion heavily damaged

---

**1:1** [...] the Watchers [...] and-they-took for-themselves wives from-all whom they-chose [...]

**1:2** [...] and-from-the-daughters-of-men [...] they-selected the-beautiful-ones [...]

**1:3** [...] and-they-descended upon Mount Hermon [...] in-the-days-of Jared [...]

**1:4** [...] and-they-bound-themselves with-mutual-oaths [...] two-hundred of-them [...]

**1:5** [...] Shemihazah who-was their-chief [...] and-Azazel [...] and-Baraq'el [...]

**1:6** [...] and-they-bore to-them giants [...] three-thousand cubits [...] was-their-height [...]

**1:7** [...] the Nephilim [...] and-the-Elioud [...] who-consumed [...]

**1:8** [...] all the-produce-of men [...] and-men could-not sustain-them [...]

**1:9** [...] and-the-earth cried-out [...] against-the-violent-ones [...]

**1:10** [...] and-its-cry ascended to-the-gates-of heaven [...]

**1:11** [...] the-giants turned against-them [...] and-devoured mankind [...]

**1:12** [...] and-they-began to-sin against birds and-beasts [...]

**1:13** [...] and-reptiles and-fish [...] and-to-devour the-flesh-of one-another [...]

**1:14** [...] and-they-drank the-blood [...]

**1:15** [...] then the-earth brought accusation against the-lawless-ones [...]

**1:16** [...] the-giants turned against-them [...] and-devoured mankind [...]

**1:17** [...] and-blood-was-shed upon the-earth [...]

**1:18** [...] and-lawlessness increased upon-it [...]

**1:19** [...] and-every-imagination of-the-thoughts of-all mankind [...]

**1:20** [...] was-only evil continually [...]

---

*EMET notes: Fragment 1 (The Watchers and Their Offspring). Source: 4Q203 frag. 7. Aramaic text from Cave 4 Qumran. Hyphenated compounds preserve Aramaic construct-chain syntax and bound morphemes. Square brackets indicate genuine manuscript lacunae where the leather has deteriorated or broken away. The Book of Giants is an Aramaic expansion of the Watcher myth from 1 Enoch 6-16, featuring the Nephilim giants Ohya, Hahya (sons of Shemihazah), Mahaway (son of Baraq'el), and the hero Gilgamesh.*
